name: Divider
summary: A thin rule that separates blocks of content — full-width, with a label, or a vertical hairline.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-divider> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens; a bare tag is a full-width rule, slotted text becomes a centred (or left/right) label, and `orientation="vertical"` is an inline hairline. Zero drift — the same element, not two look-alikes.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. The primitive is defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

spec.label: Dashed
spec.value: `dashed` swaps the rule to a dashed border

props.name: orientation
props.desc: Horizontal rule or an inline vertical hairline

props.name: align
props.desc: Where the slotted label sits along a horizontal rule

props.name: dashed
props.desc: Render the rule as a dashed line

whenToUse.when: separating stacked sections, list groups, or toolbar items
you only need consistent gaps, not a visible line
the separation reads clearly without any rule — prefer less chrome

opinion.note: A divider is quiet structure — keep it 1px and on the border token. Use a label only when the section genuinely needs naming; reach for whitespace before adding a rule.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — DS V3 has no measured Divider cell; spec derived from the token layer (border #E3E3E3 rule, text-secondary label, SemiBold 13/22 type) + AntD Divider conventions (centred label, vertical hairline). A deliberate, documented extension bound entirely to canonical tokens.
